checklist_item: Provide a precise and operational definition for the phenomenon being measured
text: What counts as eval awareness to you? For example: the model says it thinks it's being tested, it behaves differently, or it pokes around its environment. Where do you draw the line, and what would you leave out?

checklist_item: Specify the scope of the phenomenon being covered and acknowledge any excluded aspects
text: The model runs commands like `ls /` or checks today's date, but never says it thinks it's being tested. Would you count that as eval awareness? How would you score it?

checklist_item: Identify if the phenomenon has sub-components and ensure they are measured separately
text: Would you report one eval-awareness score, or a separate score for each kind (what the model says, what an LLM judge infers from reading the transcript, how the model's behaviour changes)? If you had to give one headline number, which would it be?

checklist_item: Control for unrelated tasks that may affect the results
text: You rewrite an environment to make it more realistic. The share of runs where the model says it's being tested drops from 40% to 10%. But the model also mostly stops doing the bad behaviour the environment was built to catch: that drops from 30% to 2%. What do you make of this, and what would you do next?

checklist_item: Control for unrelated tasks that may affect the results
text: You add a long, dull system prompt, and the model mentions being tested less often. What could explain this, and how would you tell the explanations apart?

checklist_item: Validate any automated output parsing techniques for accuracy, consistency and bias
text: You ask an LLM judge whether a transcript comes from a test. Suppose changing only the wording of that question moves the share of transcripts it calls tests from about 40% to almost 100%. How would you pick the wording, and what would you still trust the judge's numbers for?

checklist_item: Verify the quality and relevance of all task items especially for large or automatically generated datasets
text: Would you rather test on a few environments you built by hand, or on many that an LLM generated? If you generate them, how much would you check them before trusting the results?

checklist_item: Employ sampling strategies to ensure task items are representative of the overall task space
text: Your environments are meant to look like real use. Real use of what: coding agents, chat assistants, agents working inside a company's tools? How would you decide?

checklist_item: Include task items that test known LLM sensitivities (e.g. input permutations or variations)
text: Would you make near-copies of each environment with small changes (different names, events in a different order) to see if the results hold? How many, and what would you hope to learn?

checklist_item: If so, analyse and report the relevant strengths and limitations of the adapted prior work
text: When would you reuse test environments someone else already built, and when would you build your own?

checklist_item: If so, analyse and report the relevant strengths and limitations of the adapted prior work
text: Someone suggests putting real GitHub repos into the model's sandbox so its files look real. What are the risks, and would you do it anyway?

checklist_item: If so, report and compare performance on the new benchmark against the original
text: You take a public benchmark and edit its environments to look more realistic, and your version gets lower eval-awareness scores. What else would you need to show before saying your edits helped?

checklist_item: Investigate the potential pre-exposure of benchmark source materials or similar data in common LLM training corpora
text: Models may recognise classic safety-test setups because they've seen so many of them, like a file called `shutdown.sh` or a memo saying the model is about to be replaced. Would you swap these for ordinary situations from the domain the environment is set in, even if the new version is a less direct test of the bad behaviour?

checklist_item: Maintain a held-out set of task items to facilitate ongoing, uncontaminated evaluation
text: Would you keep your test environments private, so future models can't train on them, publish them so others can reproduce your results, or something in between? Why?

checklist_item: Implement tests to detect data contamination and apply them to the benchmark
text: How would you check whether a model already saw your environments, or ones like them, during training? Is it worth the effort?

checklist_item: Report the benchmark's sample size and justify its statistical power
text: You can afford 200 runs of the model. Would you do 10 environments with 20 runs each, or 50 environments with 4 runs each? Why?

checklist_item: Report uncertainty estimates for all primary scores to enable robust model comparisons
text: A change to your environments clearly lowers eval awareness on the environments you developed it on, but the effect is only half as large on environments you held back. How do you report it, and what do you claim?

checklist_item: Use metrics that capture the inherent variability of any subjective labels, without relying on single-point aggregation or exact matching
text: An LLM judge disagrees with you on about 1 transcript in 5 about whether the model knew it was being tested. What do you do?

checklist_item: Conduct a qualitative and quantitative analysis of common failure modes
text: When you open a transcript, what do you read first, and what are you looking for?

checklist_item: Investigate whether failure modes correlate with non-targeted phenomena (confounders) rather than the intended construct
text: A change to your environments lowers eval awareness on Claude but not on a model from another company. What would you do with that result?

checklist_item: If so, identify and discuss any potential scoring biases revealed in the error analysis
text: How do you split your time between reading individual transcripts and looking at summary numbers? When would a few odd transcripts make you doubt a clean-looking number?

checklist_item: Justify the relevance of the benchmark for the phenomenon with real-world applications
text: Does a lower eval-awareness score tell you anything about how models behave in real use? How much?

checklist_item: Discuss the limitations and design trade-offs of the benchmark concerning construct validity
text: Think of one set of eval-awareness results, your own or published ones. Give an example of a claim you'd be comfortable making from them, and a broader one you wouldn't make.

checklist_item: Discuss the limitations and design trade-offs of the benchmark concerning construct validity
text: When is it OK to make an environment more realistic at the cost of testing the behaviour less well?
